name: Detroit Zoo
tagline: Royal Oak favorite — Penguin Conservation Center, arctic animals, and a train when legs tire.

practical.ticket_note: Parking and membership deals on detroitzoo.org.
practical.best_start: Penguin Conservation Center first, then one outdoor loop (giraffes / great apes).

do_not_list.name: Elephant
do_not_list.reason: Detroit Zoo ended its elephant program in 2005; not on official animal pages 2026-08.

do_not_list.name: Hippo
do_not_list.reason: No official hippo animal page; not confirmed present.

do_not_list.name: Cheetah
do_not_list.reason: No official cheetah animal page; not confirmed present.

do_not_list.name: African penguin
do_not_list.reason: Penguin Conservation Center features macaroni (and other) penguins — do not label African penguin.

do_not_list.name: Sumatran tiger
do_not_list.reason: Official animal page is Amur tiger — use soft Tiger label or Amur, not Sumatran.

items.label: Penguin
items.one_liner: Penguin Conservation Center — waddle, dive, kid magnet.

qa_card.question: What did the penguins do in the water?
qa_card.answer: Tell a grown-up one thing you saw!

items.presence_note: NOT African penguin. Soft-label Penguin. Fix catalog_id off african-penguin.

items.label: Giraffe
items.one_liner: Tall necks above the tree line — easy wow.

qa_card.question: How tall did the giraffe seem next to you?
qa_card.answer: Tell a grown-up one thing you noticed!

items.label: Gorilla
items.one_liner: Great ape families — calm watch stop.

qa_card.question: What was the gorilla doing with its hands or face?
qa_card.answer: Tell a grown-up one thing you noticed!

items.label: African lion
items.one_liner: Pride of the grasslands — look for cubs when on view.

qa_card.question: What did you notice about the lions?
qa_card.answer: Size, sound, rest, or how they move!

items.label: Chimpanzee
items.one_liner: Smart climbers — lots of movement when active.

qa_card.question: How did the chimpanzee use its hands?
qa_card.answer: Tell a grown-up one thing you saw!

items.label: Tiger

qa_card.question: How many stripe patterns can you spot?

items.presence_note: Official is Amur tiger not Sumatran. Soft-label Tiger OK; fix catalog_id.

items.label: Red panda
items.one_liner: Tree climber — often high and hard to spot.

qa_card.question: Where was the red panda — branch or ground?
qa_card.answer: Tell a grown-up what you saw!

items.label: Polar bear
items.one_liner: Arctic icon — big and cool when on view.

qa_card.question: What color is a polar bear’s fur up close?
qa_card.answer: It can look white, cream, or yellowish!

items.label: Zebra
items.one_liner: Grevy’s zebra — bold stripes for a pattern hunt.

qa_card.question: Are any two zebras striped the same?
qa_card.answer: Each pattern is unique — like a fingerprint!

items.label: Sloth bear
items.one_liner: Shaggy bear with a long snout — fun face to watch.

qa_card.question: What does the sloth bear’s snout look like?
qa_card.answer: Long and flexible for bugs and fruit!

items.label: Warthog
items.one_liner: Tusks and a funny trot — easy laugh stop.

qa_card.question: What stood out — tusks, snout, or how it ran?

items.label: Gray wolf
items.one_liner: Pack hunter — listen for howls if they’re vocal.

qa_card.question: Did the wolf look more like a dog or something wilder?
qa_card.answer: Talk about size, ears, and how it moves!

items.presence_note: Historically present; confirm on animals-list if still exhibited

research_notes: Presence audit 2026-08-08 against detroitzoo.org animal pages (HTTP 200). Removed elephant (gone since 2005), hippo, cheetah; soft-labeled penguin/tiger/zebra. Sources: https://detroitzoo.org/animals/ and individual /animal/* pages. · presence-audit 2026-08-08 [minor]
